# Independent audit: nonregular concave-parameter volume martingale

Source read in full: `candidate 8027472c0c8717cd`, Sections 1–6. Verdict: **PASS**, with its explicitly unpenalized joint-local-minimum premise. The nonvertex conclusion in Section 5 additionally uses the stated stronger OC-bad threshold.

The exact tangent cone uses only the finitely many active extreme anchored rows. A fixed tangent direction remains feasible for a sufficiently small positive step because inactive rows have positive slack and there are finitely many rows; all entries stay positive. Multiplication by the geometric-normalizing scalar preserves the cone. The derivative of the normalized multiplier is precisely ell_p times the displayed B_p(h).

The two-stage argument is an actual local improvement. Reducing a proper base's scalar multiplier strictly reduces its attained whole-fiber maximum: if equality persisted, a maximizing point for the reduced parameter would also maximize the old parameter, and an attained old cap with a proper own trace loses a positive strip. Other fibers only lose captured mass. Supporting cuts elsewhere require no derivative. Atomic bases retain the exact old upper bound Q through fixed pure-base caps, and other bases retain their finite strict gaps by uniform continuity. Thus the intervening value is EXACTLY at most Q. If it equals Q, all its maximizers are atomic, so the separately proved hinge erosion gives a strict descent from that actual equal-value pair. Its multiplier is renormalized continuously with the new volumes. No assertion that this intervening pair is itself locally minimizing is used.

The image of the tangent cone under the finite B map is polyhedral and therefore closed. Its disjointness from the open negative orthant gives nonnegative nonzero separator coefficients, normalized to sum one. Substitution yields mu_p=sigma_p/ell_p and nu_z=w_z/ell_z with the correct sign. Testing both signs of every affine array gives equal mass and base first moment. Testing ell gives the common ell moment one. No physical response coefficients occur in this separator.

Finite Farkas writes mu-nu as a nonnegative sum of the active concavity rows e_p-lambda. With m_p=nu_p+out_p=mu_p+in_p, the absorbing transition matrix is substochastic and has absorption probability nu_p/m_p>0 at every site. Because P is finite, these probabilities have a positive common lower bound. The unique visit vector is m, and all injected mass is absorbed with target marginal exactly nu. Each transition preserves the base and ell conditionally, so optional stopping for bounded finite-state martingales gives the claimed rowwise identities. A supporting affine majorant at a source has nonnegative gap from ell; equality of its conditional expectation forces every positive target into that same contact plane.

If all positive sources are vertices, their martingale rows are identities. The positive full target then makes every point of P a vertex. Lattice completeness makes those vertices parity-distinct, since a same-parity pair would have an additional integer midpoint. The largest-fiber ordinary centroid then contradicts the stronger threshold beta<Gamma_d/k. The source correctly does not obtain this contradiction from beta<1/k alone.

The strict-contact identity-only consequence is also valid: any nontrivial conditional anchored row would violate the stipulated strict ell Jensen inequality. Then mu=nu, J=P, and sigma=w. This is a conditional conclusion, not an automatic strictness assertion.

The source correctly distinguishes its parameter separator sigma from the physical surface separator eta. Its full positive target and support-plane contacts do not imply Minkowski equality, a uniform-fiber continuous lift, or physical marginal equality. These remain separate requirements.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
